world.title: US launches fresh strikes as Iran closes Strait of Hormuz
world.summary: The United States has launched fresh military strikes following an attack on a Cyprus-flagged vessel traveling through the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global shipping. Iran has responded by closing the strategic strait, escalating tensions in the region. The incident represents a significant development in ongoing US-Iran hostilities, with potential implications for international maritime commerce and regional stability. The Strait of Hormuz is one of the world's most important oil transit routes, making any closure a matter of global economic concern.

world.title: China evacuates nearly two million people as powerful typhoon makes landfall
world.summary: China has evacuated nearly two million people as a powerful typhoon made landfall, with Zhejiang province experiencing the most severe impacts. Schools, workplaces, and outdoor activities have been suspended across the affected region, while many transport services have been cancelled. The massive evacuation represents one of the largest disaster response operations, reflecting the typhoon's significant threat to populated areas. Authorities implemented comprehensive precautionary measures to protect residents from the storm's destructive potential, including wind, flooding, and landslide risks.

world.title: US senator and close Trump ally Lindsey Graham dies after 'brief and sudden illness'
world.summary: US Senator Lindsey Graham, a 71-year-old South Carolina politician and close ally of Donald Trump, has died following a brief and sudden illness. Trump paid tribute to Graham, describing him as a "true American patriot" who will be "greatly missed." Graham was a prominent figure in Republican politics and maintained a significant influence within the Trump administration. His death marks a notable loss in the political landscape, particularly given his long tenure in the Senate and his influential role in shaping recent American foreign and domestic policy.

world.title: More than 40 kidnapped children and teachers freed after Nigerian army operation
world.summary: Nigerian armed forces successfully rescued more than 40 kidnapped children and teachers in a military operation, bringing relief to families and communities affected by the abductions. The head of the local teachers' union expressed joy and elation at the successful rescue, highlighting the emotional impact of the operation. The rescue represents a significant victory against kidnapping networks that have plagued Nigeria, particularly in northern regions. The freed individuals, including both educators and students, were returned safely, demonstrating the military's capability to conduct successful hostage recovery operations.

world.title: At least two killed in Toronto street festival shooting
world.summary: A shooting incident at a Toronto street festival resulted in at least two deaths, with police reporting an exchange of gunfire between two individuals at the event. Two firearms were recovered from the scene, indicating the involvement of armed individuals. The incident disrupted the festival and raised concerns about public safety at large outdoor gatherings. Police investigations were underway to determine the circumstances leading to the confrontation and to identify the individuals involved in the shooting exchange.

usa.title: US launches fresh strikes as Iran closes Strait of Hormuz
usa.summary: The United States military launched strikes on Iran following an Iranian attack on a Cyprus-flagged container vessel in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical global waterway. U.S. Central Command reported hitting approximately 140 targets in Iran overnight. In response, Iran claimed it had closed the Strait of Hormuz again and fired at U.S. targets in Jordan. Some Gulf states also came under attack during the escalating military confrontation. The incident represents a significant escalation in regional tensions involving major powers and threatens one of the world's most strategically important shipping routes.

usa.title: US senator and close Trump ally Lindsey Graham dies after 'brief and sudden illness'
usa.summary: Senator Lindsey Graham of South Carolina, a prominent Republican and close ally of President Donald Trump, has died at age 71 following a brief and sudden illness. Graham was a key figure on Capitol Hill who evolved from a vocal Trump critic to one of his most loyal supporters. President Trump paid tribute to the senator, describing him as a "true American patriot" who will be "greatly missed." Graham's death represents a significant loss to the Republican Party and removes an influential voice from the Senate on foreign policy and other major issues.

usa.title: Trump administration subpoenas New York Times journalists over Air Force One reporting
usa.summary: The Justice Department has subpoenaed New York Times reporters to provide grand jury testimony regarding their coverage of Air Force One, the presidential aircraft gifted to President Trump by Qatar. Federal agents appeared at journalists' homes to enforce the subpoenas, requiring testimony the following week. The reporters had published articles alleging security issues with the new plane. The action raises concerns about press freedom and government pressure on journalists covering sensitive national security matters. The incident reflects tensions between the Trump administration and major news organizations over investigative reporting.

usa.title: Landmark US housing bill becomes law despite Trump protest
usa.summary: A landmark housing bill has become law despite President Trump's opposition to the legislation. The bill aims to reduce housing costs and increase housing supply across the United States, addressing the nation's ongoing affordability crisis. Trump had wanted voter ID legislation passed before the housing law, but Congress proceeded with the housing measure. The bill's passage represents a significant legislative achievement focused on addressing housing shortages and affordability challenges facing American families. The law reflects bipartisan efforts to tackle one of the country's most pressing domestic policy issues.

usa.title: Dangerous heat wave is building, will bring oppressive temperatures to much of the United States
usa.summary: A widespread and dangerous heat wave is developing across the United States, with meteorologists warning of triple-digit temperatures expected in the Southwest and Great Plains this weekend. The extreme heat is forecast to spread eastward under a high-pressure dome that could trap oppressive temperatures for a week or longer. The heat wave poses significant health risks to vulnerable populations and threatens to strain power grids across affected regions. Meteorologists characterize the developing weather pattern as particularly dangerous, with the potential to impact much of the nation as the system moves from west to east.

india.title: Muslim judge in India faces death threats after convicting 'cow vigilantes'
india.summary: Judge Tabassum Khan has been subjected to online abuse following her conviction of 14 Hindu men in a lynching case. This incident highlights ongoing tensions in India surrounding communal violence and judicial independence. The case involves cow vigilantism, a sensitive issue in Hindu-majority India where cattle are considered sacred. The judge's conviction and subsequent harassment raise concerns about the safety of judicial officers who deliver verdicts in religiously charged cases and the broader implications for rule of law and minority protection in the country.

india.title: Tensions erupt in West Bengal after 11-year-old raped and murdered
india.summary: An 11-year-old girl's body was discovered in a pond in West Bengal, one day after her family reported her missing. The tragic incident has sparked significant tensions in the region, raising serious concerns about child safety and law enforcement response. The case has triggered widespread public outcry and protests, highlighting the persistent problem of violence against children in India. Authorities are investigating the circumstances surrounding the girl's death, which has become a focal point for discussions about protecting vulnerable populations and improving investigative procedures in such critical cases.

india.title: India is adding biofuels to petrol – but many drivers are unhappy
india.summary: India has begun blending biofuels into petrol supplies, introducing the E20 fuel blend to consumers. However, motorists have expressed significant dissatisfaction with the new fuel, reporting reduced fuel efficiency in their vehicles and concerns about increased maintenance costs. The policy aims to promote renewable energy and reduce dependence on fossil fuels, aligning with environmental sustainability goals. Despite these environmental benefits, the practical impact on vehicle performance and consumer expenses has generated considerable backlash, creating tension between government environmental objectives and public acceptance of the initiative.

india.title: Instagram running ads promoting child sexual abuse material in India, BBC finds
india.summary: The BBC has discovered that Instagram is running advertisements promoting child sexual abuse material in India. These ads use explicit terminology including "rape" and "child video" and direct users to content hosted on the messaging platform Telegram. This alarming finding reveals a significant gap in content moderation and advertising oversight on the social media platform. The discovery raises urgent questions about Meta's responsibility in preventing the spread of illegal content, protecting children from exploitation, and the effectiveness of current safeguarding mechanisms on major social media platforms operating in India.

india.title: Why an anti-sacrilege law in Punjab has sparked controversy
india.summary: Punjab's anti-sacrilege law has become a source of significant controversy, reviving one of the state's most sensitive political and religious issues ahead of state elections scheduled for next year. The legislation, designed to protect religious sentiments, has generated debate about its scope, implementation, and potential implications for religious freedom and minority rights. The timing of renewed discussions around this law reflects broader tensions between religious protection and secular governance principles in Punjab. The controversy underscores how religious legislation can become politically charged, particularly during election cycles, and highlights the delicate balance required in addressing communal sensitivities while maintaining constitutional principles.

odisha.title: Former BJD MLA Pravat Ranjan Biswal joins BJP in Odisha
odisha.summary: Former BJD (Biju Janata Dal) MLA Pravat Ranjan Biswal joined the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Bhubaneswar, marking a significant political shift in Odisha. This defection occurred shortly after the Orissa High Court declined to quash proceedings against him, suggesting potential legal pressures may have influenced his party switch. The move reflects ongoing political realignments in Odisha, where the BJD has historically dominated state politics. Biswal's transition to the BJP represents the saffron party's continued efforts to strengthen its presence in the eastern state through recruitment of established political figures from rival parties.

odisha.title: Youth killed in car-bike collision at Kandukur near Hyderabad
odisha.summary: A 21-year-old man from Odisha died in a tragic road accident when a car collided with his motorcycle at Kandukur on the outskirts of Hyderabad early Sunday morning. The incident resulted in the youth's death, prompting police to register a case against the car driver and initiate an investigation. This fatal collision highlights ongoing road safety concerns in the region and the dangers faced by two-wheeler riders in high-traffic areas. The accident underscores the need for improved traffic enforcement and awareness measures to prevent similar tragedies on busy highways connecting major metropolitan areas.

odisha.title: Five-year-high grain stocks offer India an El Niño buffer
odisha.summary: India has accumulated its largest foodgrain stockpile in five years, providing a crucial buffer against potential El Niño weather impacts on the upcoming kharif agricultural season. The substantial grain reserves position the nation to better withstand potential crop failures and supply disruptions that could result from adverse climatic conditions. This strategic stockpiling reflects India's proactive approach to food security management and agricultural risk mitigation. The reserves are particularly significant given El Niño's historical association with reduced monsoon rainfall and lower agricultural productivity, making adequate grain stocks essential for maintaining price stability and ensuring food availability across the country.

sports.title: Bellingham scores extra-time winner as England reach semi-finals
sports.summary: Jude Bellingham delivered a crucial performance for England in their World Cup quarter-final against Norway, scoring twice including an extra-time winner to secure a 2-1 comeback victory in Miami. This result propels England into the semi-finals of the tournament. Bellingham's decisive contribution, particularly his extra-time goal, proved instrumental in overcoming Norway's challenge. The victory sets up a highly anticipated semi-final clash for England as they continue their World Cup campaign with momentum on their side.

sports.title: Argentina set up England semi-final with extra-time victory over Switzerland
sports.summary: Argentina advanced to the World Cup semi-finals by defeating 10-man Switzerland 3-1 in their quarter-final match in Kansas City, with two goals coming during extra-time. This victory sets up a highly anticipated semi-final encounter between Argentina and England. Switzerland's reduction to ten men during the match proved decisive as Argentina capitalized on their numerical advantage. The result confirms that England will face Argentina in the next round, creating a significant matchup between two major football nations in the tournament's latter stages.

sports.title: McCullum sacked as England Test head coach
sports.summary: Brendon McCullum has been dismissed as England's Test head coach after four years in the position, leaving the team without both a head coach and captain. McCullum's departure marks the end of an era characterized by his distinctive 'Bazball' approach to Test cricket. The sacking follows England's series defeat against New Zealand earlier in the summer. Despite previously expressing his commitment to continuing in the role following Ben Stokes' retirement, McCullum's tenure has concluded. This decision represents a significant change in England's Test cricket leadership structure and strategy moving forward.

sports.title: Champion Sinner wary of Zverev before Wimbledon final
sports.summary: Defending Wimbledon champion Jannik Sinner faces French Open champion Alexander Zverev in the Wimbledon final, with recent history suggesting Sinner should be confident of retaining his title. However, Sinner remains cautious about Zverev's threat, recognizing the quality of his opponent. Zverev's recent success at the French Open demonstrates his current form and capability on grass courts. The matchup represents a clash between two of tennis's top players, each bringing recent Grand Slam success to the encounter. Sinner's experience as the defending champion provides some advantage, though Zverev's credentials cannot be underestimated.

sports.title: 'Finished' & 'career over' - is this the end for McGregor?
sports.summary: Conor McGregor faced Max Holloway at UFC 329 at the T-Mobile Arena, where the fight ended dramatically with McGregor hobbling out of the octagon immediately after his trademark pre-fight strut. The sudden conclusion to the bout has prompted speculation about whether this marks the end of McGregor's fighting career. McGregor's physical condition following the fight suggests a significant injury or setback occurred during the encounter. The incident has generated considerable discussion within the MMA community regarding McGregor's future in professional fighting and whether he will continue competing at the highest level.

cricket.title: Brendon McCullum removed from post as England Men's Test coach
cricket.summary: The England and Wales Cricket Board has made a significant decision to remove Brendon McCullum from his position as England Men's Test coach, marking a notable U-turn in their coaching strategy. The move appears strategically timed with the 2027 Ashes series in mind, suggesting the ECB believes a change in leadership is necessary for Test cricket preparations. McCullum will retain his role with England's white-ball teams, maintaining continuity in limited-overs cricket. This decision represents a major shift in England's Test cricket direction and reflects the ECB's assessment of their current Test performance and future objectives.

cricket.title: Heather Knight to retire from international cricket after Lord's Test
cricket.summary: England women's cricket captain Heather Knight has announced her retirement from international cricket, with her final match set to be a Test at Lord's. Knight, a World Cup-winning former England captain, joins teammate Tammy Beaumont in stepping down at the conclusion of a record-breaking career. This marks the end of an era for English women's cricket, as Knight has been a cornerstone of the national team's success and development over many years. Her retirement represents a significant transition for England women's cricket as the team looks toward future leadership and squad development.

cricket.title: Sourav Ganguly, Kevin Pietersen and Anjum Chopra inducted into ICC Hall of Fame
cricket.summary: Three cricket legends—Sourav Ganguly, Kevin Pietersen, and Anjum Chopra—have been inducted into the ICC Hall of Fame, with their names unveiled at a ceremony in Edinburgh. This prestigious recognition honors their significant contributions to international cricket across their respective careers. The inductions bring the total number of ICC Hall of Fame members to 125, reflecting the growing recognition of cricket's greatest players and personalities. These three inductees represent diverse cricket backgrounds and eras, cementing their legacies in the sport's history.

cricket.title: Buttler, Brook brilliance ensures England bulldoze India 4-0
cricket.summary: England delivered a dominant performance against India, securing a comprehensive 4-0 series victory highlighted by exceptional batting displays from Jos Buttler and Brook. India's response was hampered by a delayed start, and they failed to mount an effective challenge. A crucial second-wicket partnership of 233 runs from 103 deliveries proved decisive in establishing England's commanding position. The emphatic nature of England's victory underscores their current strength in the format and India's struggles during this tour, marking a significant result in their bilateral series.

cricket.title: Yastika Bhatia becomes first woman to hit Test century at Lord's
cricket.summary: Yastika Bhatia made history by becoming the first female batter to score a century in a women's Test match at Lord's during India's Test against England on Day 3. This milestone achievement represents a significant moment in women's cricket history, as Lord's is one of cricket's most iconic venues. Bhatia's century demonstrates the growing quality and competitiveness of women's Test cricket, while also highlighting India's strong performance in their Test series against England. The achievement underscores the progress and recognition of women's cricket on the international stage.

usa_stock.title: The stock-market rally now hinges more on AI than oil
usa_stock.summary: As earnings season commences, artificial intelligence investment has become the primary driver of stock market performance, surpassing oil's traditional influence. This shift reflects the market's growing focus on technology sector valuations and AI-related corporate investments. The transition underscores how investor sentiment has pivoted toward technology companies and their AI capabilities rather than energy sector dynamics. This fundamental change in market drivers suggests that future stock performance will increasingly depend on AI adoption rates, technological innovation, and the profitability of AI-focused enterprises rather than commodity prices or energy sector developments.

usa_stock.title: The stock market is on the verge of doing something that's never been observed in 155 years -- and it has worrisome ramifications for Wall Street
usa_stock.summary: The U.S. stock market is approaching an unprecedented event in its 155-year history, with potentially concerning implications for Wall Street. This historic development represents a significant departure from established market patterns and cycles. The article suggests this anomaly carries troubling consequences for financial institutions and market participants. While specific details remain undisclosed in the snippet, the unprecedented nature of this occurrence and its negative ramifications indicate a fundamental shift in market dynamics or valuation metrics that warrants investor attention and could reshape traditional investment strategies and risk management approaches.

usa_stock.title: The US stock market is becoming 'too big to fail'
usa_stock.summary: The U.S. stock market is reaching a scale where systemic importance may prevent prolonged bear markets from occurring. This development suggests that market size and interconnectedness with the broader economy have created conditions where extended downturns become increasingly unlikely. The concept of markets being "too big to fail" implies that policymakers and institutions may intervene to prevent severe market declines, similar to financial crisis prevention measures. This structural shift could fundamentally alter historical market cycles and investor expectations regarding downside risk, potentially creating moral hazard concerns while simultaneously providing a floor for market valuations during periods of economic stress.

usa_stock.title: Stocks rally when Congress goes on summer break. Here's why
usa_stock.summary: Stock prices experience greater volatility when lawmakers are actively engaged in legislative sessions, with regulatory uncertainty being the primary driver of this increased market fluctuation. Conversely, when Congress takes summer recess, stocks tend to rally as investors face reduced uncertainty regarding potential regulatory changes or legislative actions. This pattern demonstrates how political activity directly influences market behavior through the creation of policy-related uncertainty. The relationship between congressional activity and market performance highlights investors' sensitivity to regulatory risk and their preference for periods of legislative inactivity, suggesting that political calendars significantly impact equity valuations and trading patterns throughout the year.

usa_stock.title: Majority of U.S. workers support an AI wealth fund as tech layoffs surge, survey finds
usa_stock.summary: A majority of U.S. employees now support the creation of an AI sovereign wealth fund to increase corporate accountability, according to recent survey data, amid rising technology sector layoffs. This growing support reflects worker concerns about the distribution of AI-generated wealth and the employment impacts of artificial intelligence adoption. The survey indicates public sentiment favoring mechanisms to ensure corporations share benefits from AI advancement with workers affected by technological displacement. This development suggests potential political momentum for policies addressing AI-related job losses and wealth concentration, potentially influencing future regulatory frameworks and corporate governance standards in the technology sector.

ai.title: Anthropic found a hidden space where Claude puzzles over concepts
ai.summary: Anthropic has developed a technique called the Jacobian lens that provides unprecedented insight into how large language models function internally. The tool allows researchers to observe what happens inside Claude as it answers questions and performs tasks, revealing findings that range from mundane to concerning. This breakthrough represents the clearest glimpse yet at the inner workings of LLMs, offering potential implications for understanding AI behavior, safety, and interpretability. The discovery could help researchers better understand how these models process information and make decisions.

ai.title: OpenAI wants its new tool to do your work for you and with you
ai.summary: OpenAI has rebranded its Codex tool to offer independent workflows capable of running autonomously for extended periods. The new tool is designed to both perform work independently and collaborate with users on tasks. This represents a significant evolution in AI capabilities, moving toward more autonomous AI agents that can handle complex workflows without constant human intervention. The development reflects the broader industry shift toward agentic AI systems that can operate with greater independence while maintaining the ability to work alongside human users.

ai.title: Humanoid robots controlled by surgeons did world-first operation on live pigs
ai.summary: Surgeons have successfully conducted the world's first operation using humanoid robots controlled remotely, performing the procedure on live pigs in a preclinical trial. This milestone demonstrates the feasibility of deploying humanoid robots in surgical settings, combining advanced robotics with remote human expertise. The successful operation represents a significant step toward practical applications of humanoid robots in healthcare, potentially expanding surgical capabilities and enabling remote surgical interventions. The preclinical trial validates the technology's potential for future medical applications.

ai.title: Hackers can use 9 of the most popular AI tools to assemble massive botnets
ai.summary: Security researchers have discovered that hackers can exploit nine of the most popular AI tools to construct large-scale botnets through a technique called "HalluSquatting," which weaponizes LLMs' inability to acknowledge when they lack information. This vulnerability allows attackers to manipulate AI systems into providing malicious instructions by exploiting their tendency to generate plausible-sounding but false responses. The discovery highlights a critical security gap in widely-used AI platforms, demonstrating how fundamental limitations in language model design can be weaponized for cybercriminal purposes.

ai.title: Facing US export controls, China's DeepSeek plans to make its own chips
ai.summary: In response to US export restrictions on advanced semiconductors, China's DeepSeek AI company is developing plans to manufacture its own chips to reduce dependency on Nvidia and Huawei. This strategic move reflects the geopolitical tensions surrounding AI technology and semiconductor access, with China seeking to build domestic capabilities to circumvent American export controls. The initiative represents a significant effort to establish Chinese technological independence in AI infrastructure, potentially reshaping the global AI chip market and intensifying competition between US and Chinese AI development.

quantum.title: Researchers Reveal the Power of 'Quantum Proofs'
quantum.summary: Researchers have demonstrated that verifying solutions to certain computational problems inherently requires grappling with quantum complexity. This finding reveals fundamental limitations in classical verification methods, showing that quantum mechanics cannot be bypassed when checking the correctness of solutions to specific problem classes. The research highlights how quantum effects are not merely incidental but essential to understanding computational verification processes, with implications for cryptography, algorithm design, and our theoretical understanding of what can be efficiently verified in computational systems.

quantum.title: Quantum error correction can constantly recalibrate a processor
quantum.summary: Researchers have developed a quantum error correction approach that uses reinforcement learning to continuously recalibrate quantum processors by leveraging error information. Rather than treating errors as static problems, the system dynamically adjusts control algorithms based on accumulated error data, improving processor performance over time. This advancement addresses a critical challenge in quantum computing: maintaining qubit stability and accuracy. By implementing adaptive recalibration strategies, the technique represents progress toward more reliable and practical quantum computers, potentially accelerating the timeline for quantum systems to achieve useful computational advantages in real-world applications.

quantum.title: Scientists' Side Hustle? Using AI and Quantum Computing to Generate New Peptides
quantum.summary: Researchers have demonstrated how quantum computing combined with artificial intelligence can accelerate the discovery and development of new peptides for pharmaceutical applications. By securing funding and dedicating time to this interdisciplinary effort, scientists showed quantum computing's potential in drug development targeting underserved populations and rare diseases. The approach leverages quantum computing's ability to explore molecular configurations more efficiently than classical methods, while AI optimizes the search process. This collaboration highlights emerging opportunities for quantum technology in healthcare innovation, particularly for addressing medical needs in populations with limited treatment options.

quantum.title: Quantum is the future for Washington. Inside a White House summit.
quantum.summary: Quantum technology has emerged as a U.S. national security priority following China's designation of quantum computing as one of its seven strategic future industries. The White House has convened a summit to address quantum's critical importance to American competitiveness and defense capabilities. This governmental focus reflects growing recognition that quantum computing represents a transformative technology with significant geopolitical implications. The summit discussions likely centered on accelerating domestic quantum research, securing supply chains, and developing workforce capabilities. The shift underscores how quantum computing has transitioned from academic research to a matter of national strategic importance in the U.S.-China technological competition.

quantum.title: We Know Simple Fluids Can Flow. Turns Out, Some Can Fracture.
quantum.summary: Researchers have discovered that certain simple, non-elastic fluids can fracture and break apart, challenging the long-held assumption that only complex elastic fluids possess this capability. Scientists previously believed elasticity was the essential property enabling fluid fracturing, but this new finding contradicts that theory. The observation of cracks forming in nonelastic simple fluids suggests a more nuanced understanding of fluid mechanics is needed. This discovery has implications for materials science, engineering applications involving fluid behavior, and fundamental physics. The research may reshape how scientists classify and predict fluid behavior under stress, potentially affecting industries relying on fluid dynamics and material processing.

trump.title: US senator and close Trump ally Lindsey Graham dies after 'brief and sudden illness'
trump.summary: Senator Lindsey Graham, a 71-year-old South Carolina Republican and one of President Trump's closest allies in Congress, has died following a brief and sudden illness. Graham was an influential voice on national security and foreign policy who traveled globally advocating for aggressive U.S. foreign policy positions. President Trump paid tribute to Graham, calling him a "true American patriot" who will be "greatly missed." Graham's death marks a significant loss for the Trump administration and the Republican Party, as he was a key congressional ally and advisor to the president.

trump.title: Trump administration subpoenas New York Times journalists over Air Force One reporting
trump.summary: The Trump administration has subpoenaed four New York Times journalists who reported on alleged security issues with the president's new Air Force One aircraft, which was gifted by Qatar. The reporters received legal summons after publishing their investigation into potential vulnerabilities with the plane. The subpoenas represent an escalation in tensions between the Trump administration and the media over national security reporting. The incident raises questions about press freedom and the administration's approach to handling critical coverage of sensitive government matters and presidential security protocols.

trump.title: Landmark US housing bill becomes law despite Trump protest
trump.summary: A landmark housing bill has become law despite President Trump's opposition to the legislation. The president had wanted voter ID legislation passed before the housing law, which aims to reduce housing costs and increase supply across the nation. The bill's passage represents a significant legislative achievement despite Trump's protest, indicating that Congress proceeded with the measure even without presidential support. The housing legislation addresses affordability and supply challenges in the U.S. real estate market, representing a major policy initiative that advanced through the legislative process independent of the administration's preferred legislative priorities.

trump.title: Trump threatens to 'decimate and destroy' Iran if they try to kill him
trump.summary: President Trump has threatened to "decimate and destroy" Iran if the country attempts to assassinate him, stating that plans are in place to respond to any such threat. The threat comes amid escalating tensions between the United States and Iran, including recent U.S. military strikes and Iranian actions affecting critical waterways. Trump's warning represents a significant escalation in rhetoric regarding U.S.-Iran relations and reflects heightened security concerns surrounding the president. The statement underscores the volatile geopolitical situation and the administration's aggressive posture toward Iran during this period of international tension.

trump.title: Trump-appointed judge permanently ends Proud Boys Jan. 6 case, says Constitution left him no choice
trump.summary: A Trump-appointed federal judge has permanently dismissed the convictions of four Proud Boys leaders related to January 6 Capitol riot charges, stating the Constitution left him no choice in the ruling. Despite granting the dismissal, the judge sharply rebuked the Capitol riot as an attack on democracy. The decision represents a significant legal development in cases stemming from the January 6, 2021 Capitol riot, with implications for other similar prosecutions. The ruling highlights ongoing judicial debates over constitutional interpretation regarding the charges brought against Capitol riot participants and reflects the complex legal landscape surrounding January 6 accountability.

local.title: 322,000 Californians sign up to have data brokers delete their personal information
local.summary: Over 322,000 Californians have enrolled in a program requiring data brokers to delete their personal information and cease future data collection and sales. This initiative represents a significant privacy protection effort, allowing residents to exercise control over their sensitive data. The program mandates that data brokers not only purge existing information but also refrain from collecting and selling any future data associated with participating individuals. This development reflects growing consumer awareness and legislative action regarding data privacy rights, particularly in California, which has been at the forefront of implementing stringent data protection regulations to safeguard residents' personal information from commercial exploitation.

local.title: Every pick from the 2026 MLB Draft Day 1: Scouting analysis and evaluations
local.summary: The 2026 MLB Draft's first day featured an expanded format with four complete rounds and 135 total picks, representing a significant increase from traditional draft structures. The New York Times provided comprehensive scouting analysis and evaluations of each selection, examining player prospects and their potential impact on professional baseball. The first round proceeded with somewhat predictable outcomes, though the expanded format allowed teams to select additional prospects. This supersized Day 1 structure demonstrates baseball's evolving approach to talent acquisition and development, giving more players opportunities to be selected while providing teams with expanded roster-building capabilities during the crucial opening day of the draft process.

local.title: Scientists Explain How to Protect Yourself Amid Explosive Diarrhea Outbreak
local.summary: A significant diarrhea outbreak is affecting communities, prompting scientific guidance on protective measures and prevention strategies. Health experts have provided recommendations for individuals to safeguard themselves during the outbreak. The condition presents serious health concerns, with symptoms potentially persisting for weeks if left untreated, underscoring the importance of proper medical intervention. Scientists emphasize the need for preventive action and appropriate treatment to avoid prolonged illness. The outbreak highlights public health vulnerabilities and the critical role of scientific communication in helping populations respond effectively to infectious disease threats, particularly regarding gastrointestinal illnesses that can cause significant morbidity if not properly managed.
